title: Arrays with $unwind
idea: `$unwind` splits an array field into one document per element, so later stages can match, sort or group the elements individually.
points: Each new document copies the original, with `items` replaced by one element.
Name the array with a `$` path: `{ $unwind: '$items' }`.
A `$match` after `$unwind` tests one element at a time.
`$size` counts an array's elements without splitting; `$push` collects values back into an array.

steps.caption: Two orders reach `$unwind: '$items'`. Each holds an `items` array with two elements.
The first order becomes two documents, one per element. Both keep `total: 120`.
The second order splits the same way. Now every document holds one `items` object, not an array.
`$group` by `'$items.sku'` merges the two pen lines. Book and lamp stay alone.

code.title: Split, group, count
code.caption: Three pipelines on the shared data. Step through them, then press Run.

walk.text: Keep Ana's orders, then split each into one document per `items` element.
`$project` keeps two fields and hides `_id`. The next page covers it.
Sort for a fixed order. `'items.sku'` is a path into the element.
Unwind every order, then group by the element's `sku`.
`$sum` adds element fields: `qty` for units, and `$multiply` of `qty` and `price` for revenue.
No unwind here: `$size` counts each order's elements, and `$sum` totals them per customer.

pitfalls: Sum element fields, not parent fields: `total` repeats once per element after `$unwind`.
`$unwind` drops documents whose array is empty, missing or null, unless `preserveNullAndEmptyArrays: true`.
After `$unwind`, read element fields as `'$items.sku'`; `'$sku'` is missing and groups under `null`.

quiz.why: Ben has two orders with 1 and 2 items. `$unwind` makes one document per element: 1 + 2 = 3.

takeaway: Unwind to work per element, then group to fold the pieces back.
